episode.title: 898: An Argument
episode.description:
Nikole Hannah-Jones made an argument 10 years ago in The New York Times Magazine that became famous. She wrote about choosing a public school for her daughter, Najya, in one of the most racially and economically segregated school systems in the country: New York City. Nikole chose a regular public school, one that most wealthy and middle-class parents wouldn’t consider, and she challenged other parents to do the same.  She revisits that argument, and that choice, in a series of conversations with producer Chana Joffe-Walt and with her daughter, Najya, who’s now 16 and has her own very different views. 

Visit thisamericanlife.org/lifepartners to sign up for our premium subscription.

(00:00:00) Prologue: Chana talks with Nikole about what they both remember from being young parents just starting to think about schools for their children. (9 minutes)

(00:10:44) Act One: Nikole talks with Chana about Najya’s elementary school and the problems her family navigated there. (15 minutes)

(00:25:00) Act Two: Chana talks with Najya about her memories of elementary and middle school and how she felt about her mom’s choices. (9 minutes)

(00:31:45) Act Three: Nikole and Najya talk about what changed when Najya pushed back against her mom’s choices for elementary and middle school and got to choose her own high school. (10 minutes)

(00:42:16) Act Four: Nikole and Najya talk with each other about the different choices they made and the questions they still have for each other. (9 minutes)

(00:51:13) Act Five: Nikole fact-checks her memory against her old emails with Najya’s elementary school and has a painful revelation. (7 minutes)

episode.title: S9E9 鲁豫对话刘索拉 | 一生不断找北，直到天高地广
episode.description:
– 本节目由GIADA出品 –

【本期制作人】阿萌

【本期嘉宾】

刘索拉，作曲家，作家

陈鲁豫，媒体人、主持人

【本期节目介绍】

岩中花述第九季第九期，鲁豫见到了一头银发的刘索拉。她正从一场漫长的疾病中慢慢恢复。曾经，她可以持续创作与演出，如今一天只能工作约一个小时。状态最差时，她每一秒都在对付身体，音乐与文学都无法让她从中抽离。

刘索拉学作曲出身，她所在的中央音乐学院作曲系77/78级聚集了谭盾、陈其钢、郭文景、叶小纲、周龙、陈怡等后来享誉国际的作曲家。她回忆，1977年恢复高考后，大家像是「压抑了太久」。一批有才华的人结伴而来，成为中国当代音乐史上的华章。

但她却先在文学上获得声名。1985年，《你别无选择》发表于《人民文学》，这部以中央音乐学院作曲系学生为原型的小说，让她成为80年代极受关注的年轻作家。

几年后，她在音乐上取得了同样的关注，专辑《蓝调在东方》与《中国拼贴》在世界音乐界惊艳亮相。至今，文学与音乐两道路仍在她的人生延伸。

她始终与主流保持距离，抗拒作品带来的关注，因为「特别背叛初衷」。小说出名，她埋头做音乐。唱片公司希望她写更容易被接受的音乐，她扭头离开。音乐在世界得到认可，她决定回国。她形容这是「找北」——「找了点小北，再往前走走。」

童年时期，她是每天能吃一斤奶糖的小孩。父母宠爱她，钢琴、京剧、影视、文学很早进入她的生活。

11岁时，生活骤然改变，她经历冷眼与伤怀，她穿着故意弄破的中山装上街，想要「对抗社会」。她说自己学会了「轻视」，所以「什么都不怕。」

她曾相信相爱和婚姻会共同搭起一座完美的「粉色小房子」，两个人可以一直住在里面。但现在她坚持「成熟人的关系应该是聪明和酷的关系。」

30岁时，她渴望60岁。真正走过60岁，她不再染白发，更觉「天高地广」。曾经，她「坚决不要」家里有花，现在也让人在花园里种起了花，因为「看着喜庆」。

她重新开始写音乐，也重新开始写作，等身体再好一些，她就请朋友们来吃饭。

她还在朝北走去。

episode.title: Dad, I’m going to Ukraine
episode.description:
We meet Condor, which is not his real name. It’s his military call sign. Condor was an IT specialist back home but, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, he felt an unexplainable pull to join the fight alongside Ukrainian soldiers. It’s a decision that shocked his friends and his family. He’s now been in the country for three years, and even he still struggles sometimes to understand why he enlisted.  


Condor is among the thousands of Latin American soldiers who have joined Ukraine’s fight against Russia. He and his comrades spend weeks in the trenches, rifle in hand, prepared to kill — and to be killed. Their reasons for going vary, but through Condor’s story we gain insight into why these men and women leave everything behind, and travel to a country far away to fight in a war that is not their own. 

From LA Times Studios and DW, in collaboration with Futuro Studios, this four-part series is available in English and Spanish.

episode.title: Vol.276 做月嫂育儿嫂的姐姐，都有故事
episode.description:
英语里有一句俗语，it takes a village to raise a child。意思就是养育需要整个社会的支持。这个理念落到中国城市的实际中，其实并不那么田园牧歌。在现有的产假制度，以及社会的幼儿养育服务基础下，一个城市里的双职工夫妻，想要仅靠自己的时间和精力承担起养育孩子的大部分工作，很难。 他们往往需要依靠父母的支持，或是购买购买服务，很多时候是两者兼有。

所谓购买服务，其实就是请阿姨。阿姨其实是一个非常有中国特色和时代特色的名词。一些在中国工作的外国人，都会直接把它翻译成拼音“ayi”。这说明他们觉得这个概念无法直接用nanny等单词指代（类似的例子还有guanxi）。

从商业的角度看，为城市家庭寻找合适的阿姨，是一件极其刚需，又极难做好的事情。因为它缺乏公共领域的共识、知识和信任体系。每个人的决策都充满了偶然。因为这是一门人的因素极高的生意，也因此充满故事。

本期的嘉宾仪婷巧合之下走入家政顾问行业。用她的话说，这个过程让她与此前从未有交集的人建立了联系，也让她对中国城市家庭有了新的认知。

爱哲按：

2010 年的夏天，我正在南方周末北京站实习，编辑部当时讨论的最多的一个选题，就是富士康工人连续跳楼事件。当时全国的媒体都在关注和报道这一系列的惨剧，这些报道让人们，包括我自己，第一次了解到制造业工人的处境。

而今天这期节目的讲述者占有兵，当时就在这样一家工厂里工作。

占有兵：当时认真考虑过这件事。流水线通过细分工序，提高制造效率的稳定性，同时也增强了人员的可替代性。换句话说，换谁来都能做，换谁来都做得一样好。虽然当时还没有实现机器自动化，可是人的价值几乎就不太重要了。

你可能不认识占有兵，但你可能看过占有兵拍的照片。打工的人，工厂的车间，密密麻麻的床铺和生活用品，这些照片里的图景，都是占有兵生活和工作的地方，他当时就是这些工人中的一员。

episode.description: 去年8月24日晚上9點多，馬偕淡水急診專科醫師鄭筆方正在打病歷，左肩突然痠麻無力。他替自己做了一次神經學檢查，轉頭告訴護理師：「我好像中風了，幫我量血壓、血糖，等一下我如果昏倒，請告訴後面的醫生」。話說完沒多久，他就失去意識。 醒來時人在加護病房，左側肢體肌力只剩一分，連翻身都做不到。從站在床邊的人，變成躺在床上的人。 這集來賓是鄭筆方醫師，新書《醫生壞掉以後：急診醫師的中風自救處方》。他把這半年當成一份試驗報告來寫：哪些復健真的有用、哪些只是維持、健保和長照的資源怎麼銜接、家屬該問醫院什麼。經過半年復健後，他重回急診室救人，第一天就正確診斷了一位盲腸炎病人。 【聽完這集你會知道】 03:48｜FAST口訣，四個字判斷中風 臉歪、單側手腳無力或麻、講話含糊，記下第一個症狀出現的時間。不要以為是太累，休息一下就好，這一躺就錯過了。 05:07｜為什麼一定要打119，不要自己去醫院 不是每家急診都能處理中風、施打血栓溶解劑，有些甚至沒有神經內科醫師。只有119知道該送你去哪一家。 17:14｜被動運動只是維持，一對一才能喚醒 手搖機、腳踏車都是好手好腳帶著壞手壞腳動，防止萎縮而已。要從不能動到能動，需要一對一的神經物理與職能治療誘發。住院期間也可以自費另請老師。 22:37｜資源地圖：復健病房計畫、PAC、長照3.0 健保署新的復健病房示範計畫針對中風一個月內、有強烈復健意願的病人，最長180天。出院之後再由長照3.0的居家復能銜接。 30:34｜想找教練加強，要先請醫師劃好邊界 中風是特殊族群，一般健身房練過頭反而張力上升。順序是醫師定血壓心率的邊界，物理職能老師定運動種類，教練才在範圍內執行。 【本集金句】 「我不甘心我往後的二、三十年都是躺在床上度過。」 #鄭筆方 #醫生壞掉以後 #中風復健 #FAST口訣 #長照3.0 主持人：《慢老》作者 黃惠如 來賓：馬偕紀念醫院淡水分院急診專科醫師 鄭筆方 製作團隊：錢玉紘、劉駿逸 ＊訂閱天下全閱讀：https://bit.ly/3STpEpV ＊下載天下雜誌App：https://bit.ly/3ELcwhX ＊意見信箱：bill@cw.com.tw -- Hosting provided by SoundOn

episode.description:
Brian Rudolph started making chickpea pasta in his Detroit apartment because wheat made him feel sick. A decade later, Banza was in more than 25,000 stores, and today, it’s one of the most popular pasta brands in the country. Success was not automatic: The business barely got off the ground because the cooked pasta was turning to mush—and as Banza became known for its health benefits, a food-safety scare sent sales plunging by 30%.

In this episode, Brian explains why he was inspired to create a whole new category, how he turned chickpea skeptics into fans, and how the company rebuilt trust after a public relations disaster. 

What you’ll learn 

  • How Brian and his brother Scott launched Banza with only $100,000.
  • How they learned to stop chasing perfection and to ship something that was “good enough.” 
  • How crowdfunding and reality TV helped Banza land its first retail accounts. 
  • How packaging can become an important growth engine for a new brand. 
  • How transparency can rebuild trust after a PR debacle–but can’t restore it overnight.

episode.title: EP88 史上最强播客/读书笔记？
episode.description:
事实上，这套笔记系统适用所有流过你大脑的信息，无论信息从什么地方来。而且每天只需10分钟。

记笔记的最大痛点是什么？

在之前的征集中，集中在这两点上：1️⃣ 笔记记了很多，但用不起来（都忘了/用的时候无法调取）；2️⃣ 笔记很零碎，无法形成一个完整的知识体系。

之所以产生这些痛点，是因为：你试图用「考试型笔记」，去满足「成长」的诉求。

我们做事要以终为始、目的导向。考试型笔记的目的是提高考试成绩，它的特点就是要囊括所有重要的知识点、要知道知识点如何「在理论上」使用、要有整个知识点的架构，通常按照章节、题型、知识分类来组织笔记。这样你才能反复背诵，以期覆盖更多考点。

但成长不是为了考试啊？

成长型笔记，必须要围绕「成长」这个目的来设计。它必须满足三个条件：轻量（所以能长期持续，成为自己人生OS的一部分）、可实操（不能知行合一的不叫真正的成长）、个性化（每一个人的成长都是独特的、不存在标准答案或模板）。

我们必须让这个笔记实现一个「淘金」的效果：每天各种信息像沙海一样从你的脑中流过，经过你的这个笔记系统的过滤，只留下几颗金砂。这些金砂会化为成长的种子，进入你的认知森林，成为生态的一部分，并体现为你整个人的改变。

今天就给大家讲讲，什么是成长型笔记，它应该长啥样。

我把这套笔记命名为：破·立·行。

episode.title: EP59 上官婉儿与武曌：从赏识，到背叛
episode.description:
- 导语 -

一个让你家族覆灭的人，也给了你施展才华的机会，你会如何面对她？

对于上官婉儿而言，武曌就是这样一个人。祖父上官仪因卷入废后风波被杀，尚在襁褓中的她随母亲没入掖庭。十余年后，她凭借出众的文才获得武曌赏识，开始走近帝国的权力中心。家族的命运曾因武曌而改变，她自己的未来，也与武曌紧紧相连。

但从被赏识到被信任，还有多远？成为高宗的“才人”，意味着做皇帝的嫔妃，还是皇后的秘书？跟随武曌十八年，为何直到三十余岁，她才真正走入决策核心圈？而那道留在脸上的伤痕，究竟源于后世津津乐道的争风吃醋，还是触碰了权力不能容忍的界限？

这一期，我们循着正史、墓志与宫廷传闻，走近上官婉儿与武曌之间复杂的关系，也看见她们身旁那些草拟诏令、参与政事，却鲜少留下姓名的女性。当才华让一个女子获得了接近权力的机会，她能否也因此获得选择的自由？武曌给了上官婉儿施展野心的机会，也为她的野心设下了天花板。

当皇帝走向生命的终点，这份依附于个人的权力又能延续多久？面对自己的未来，上官婉儿将如何重新选择？在背叛的背后，有一个不愿随武曌一同退场的上官婉儿。

——Leo & Sophia

-《两步之遥》时间的约定 -

恭喜以下10位听友达成“《两步之遥》时间的约定”成就：回昔叙、温带海鲜气候、葳蕤紫苜蓿、点五人、尤莉卡、Ssoba、一根废竹、Azure-薇薇、Yuki0821、一代宗师。

让我们恭喜他们！

也请还没有被念到，以及还没有解锁这个挑战的听友也不要着急。时光漫漫，我们有耐心和信心一直一起走下去......

episode.title: The Ultimate Guide to Divorce (For You & The People You Love)
episode.description:
You wouldn't believe the amount of times Mel has asked to do an episode on divorce

And finally….here it is:

The ULTIMATE guide on how to handle divorce - for you and the people you love.

Whether you’ve been through a divorce, are thinking about one, are going through one now, have a loved one you need to support, or are the child of divorced parents, this episode is a resource.

World renowned divorce lawyer James Sexton is back to break down divorce from every imaginable angle, and give takeaways that you can implement today regardless of where you are in what he calls divorce’s “six stages”.

James will tell you the five situations where he believes divorce may be necessary, how to tell your spouse the marriage is over, and the 48 hour plan you should have in place before you do.

You’ll also learn how to protect yourself financially, how to choose the right attorney, and how to stop the need for “revenge” from costing you money.

James also addresses “staying together for the kids,” explains how a divorce ends a marriage and not a family, and why your decision on whether to have a divorce or not affects your kids even more than you know.

You’ll learn:

-The 6 stages of divorce and what to do during each one

-Who you should — and should not — talk to when you’re considering divorce

-What financial documents and information you need to protect yourself

-The biggest mistake people make once they’re in the middle of a divorce

-Why trying to “win” your divorce can destroy your future

-How to set goals for your post-divorce life before emotions take over

-Why you should get a therapist before you get a dating app

-How to rebuild your identity and your life after divorce

-The best way to support someone you love who is going through a divorce

James says “The grief isn't evidence that the marriage failed, it means it mattered.” 

If you are dealing with divorce yourself, this episode will help you understand where you are and what may be next. 

If someone you love is going through a divorce, you will learn how to show up in a way that is meaningful.

Either way, the more informed you are, the better you can navigate it.
